result.title: Vis2State: Visual Reasoning through Executable State Abstractions
result.summary: Solving visual puzzles requires both accurate interpretation of visual evidence and reliable computation under task-specific rules. Embedding visual assumptions and task constraints directly in solving code makes the represented problem difficult to inspect and revise independently. We introduce Vis2State, a training-free agentic framework that abstracts visual puzzles into explicit, revisable problem states linking visual inspection and execution. Visual inspection guides state construction and refinement, while generated programs solve the represented problem. The model constructs both the state and the program without predefined puzzle schemas or solving procedures. Inspection and execution feedback allow it to revise the problem representation and solving procedure independently. Vis2State achieves the state-of-the-art performance on four benchmarks. Cross-model evaluation further demonstrates consistent gains. Ablations, error analyses, and fixed-program state interventions further support the effectiveness of the state-centered design. The code will be made publicly available to facilitate future research.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练 agentic 框架 Vis2State，将视觉谜题抽象为可检查、可修订的显式问题状态，由视觉检查指导状态构建，再由生成程序执行并借助反馈分别修订表示与求解过程。
AI.relevance_reason: 其显式状态与独立修订机制可作为 latent 推理工作区的对照，状态干预和错误分析可供核查视觉证据筛选、表示修订及执行反馈对推理状态与停止决策的影响。
